issues.reason: Korean 앞으로 보내요 literally suggests forward, but tense-backshift context requires earlier/back-in-time. Native translations clearly say move one step back, matching the assessed reported-speech tense relation.
Stative-progressive restriction and cleft-pronoun that/who/which descriptions require expert qualification. Particularly which as a cleft marker is register-sensitive; no teacher approval asserted.

Both no matter how ~ and however ~ are English learning targets; canonical Korean copula 이에요 frames their equivalence. Native wording now explicitly states same meaning, and role is localized_instruction_or_meaning. No target phrase was translated away.
Parallelism/agreement/comparative-superlative hints are context-bound simplified rules. Presence of the/in Korea alone is not a universal superlative test.
Native wording explicitly scopes -ing after to to THIS to in look forward to, avoiding a false general rule for all to.

Passage directly states more talking after phone rule; improved focus is an inferred purpose/benefit, not a separately measured result. Source explanation retains that broader inference; no new efficacy evidence asserted.
